registered_before: any LID-DS scenario image runs on the cluster; images are being built on .234 from github.com/LID-DS/LID-DS (commit 5b8e414) and no build result has been read for the design below
owner_decision: 13/11: the owner approved running the real CVEs of LID-DS on the cluster
purpose: close weakness W2 (notes/PAPER_PLAN.md): the live campaign so far used self-written fixtures that always start with a kubectl exec. Here the 15 LID-DS 2021 scenarios run on Kubernetes under the token probe: real vulnerable services, their own normal clients and their own exploits, the exploit acting inside the service's process tree. Same model, alphabet, threshold rule and decision as lidds-ml-v5; the lineage tag (ml-final-study-v1 amendment 2) is recorded
scenarios: every scenario whose victim, normal and exploit images build from the repository unchanged and whose victim passes its own availability check (main.py wait_for_availability) on the cluster; each exclusion is written with its reason before the capture starts. No scenario is chosen or dropped after the capture

isolation.namespace: lidds-live, not in the Istio ambient mesh
isolation.network: NetworkPolicy: ingress only from pods of the same namespace; egress only to pods of the same namespace and to the cluster DNS; no Service of type NodePort or LoadBalancer, no Ingress
isolation.images: built on .234 and imported into containerd of the workers; imagePullPolicy Never
isolation.teardown: the namespace and the images are deleted when the analysis has read the run

cycle.definition: one cycle per scenario: the victim pod is recreated, its availability check passes, warm-up 30 s, then a 150 s recording span; the scenario's normal users act through the whole cycle
cycle.users: per scenario as its main.py: a user count drawn uniformly from 3 to 20 per cycle, wait times from the LID-DS sampler ('usask', timerange_sampling over the cycle length), the command of the scenario's normal image (stdin line or exec) sent at each wait time
cycle.exploit: in an exploit cycle the scenario's exploit command(s) run once at a time drawn uniformly in [30 %, 80 %] of the recording span, as main.py; the exploit time is the time the driver sends the command
cycle.seeds: schedule seed 20261113 for user counts, wait times, exploit cycles and exploit times; the schedule is written before the live phase starts and is not read by the worker

phases.capture: 12 h of normal cycles only, every scenario in parallel; the worker records token windows (no model)
phases.fit: token_branch_fit.py with the registered cluster settings of lidds-ml-v5 (5-fold cross-fit over contiguous 30 min chunks, held-out 60 s block maxima, moment Gumbel without the top 1 %, alpha' = 0.00018), one model per victim workload, from the capture only
phases.live: 12 h; each cycle is an exploit cycle with probability 0.5 (seeded); the worker scores every victim window with the fitted model and threshold

metrics.detected: an exploit cycle with an alarm window of the victim ending in [exploit time, exploit time + 30 s]
metrics.latency: end of the first such window minus the exploit time; and kernel to Alertmanager when the bridge runs
metrics.false_alarm_cycle: a normal cycle (no exploit) with an alarm window ending in its recording span (warm-up excluded, as LID-DS records after warm-up)
metrics.warm_up_alarms: alarms in the warm-up of every cycle are reported separately (the victim's own start)
metrics.lineage: per scenario, the share of alarm windows whose surprising grams are on the native lineage; H2 of ml-final-study-v1 amendment 2 is read here: native-stream detection of the exploit cycles

expectations.recall: >= 95 % pooled over the scenarios that lidds-ml-v5 detects at 100 % on LID-DS 2021 official, and reported per scenario
expectations.note: a scenario whose exploit leaves no trace in the dataset (Juice-Shop) is reported, not pooled into the recall expectation; nothing is tuned after the capture

limits: the scenarios' traffic generators are the dataset's, not production traffic; one victim replica per scenario; the cluster is shared by the AIMS workloads, which keep running and are not scored here; the run uses the probe build with the lineage tag
code: scripts/lidds_live/ (Kubernetes manifests, image import, driver), sentinel_pulse/collector (namespace allow-list), scripts/analysis/pulse_live_lidds.py
